channel.title: California Uzbek — Latest
channel.description: Independent analysis · Central Asia & world geopolitics

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva to Represent Uzbekistan at the 81st UN General Assembly
item.description: The head of Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration is taking part in the general debate in New York and met UN Secretary-General António Guterres.

item.title: Gaza's School Year Opens in Tents: 541,000 Students Return
item.description: Per the Palestinian Ministry of Education, about 541,000 students returned to education on 19 September 2026. UNICEF says ~98% of school buildings are damaged; most learning is in tents and damaged classrooms.

item.title: How to read the news: media literacy basics
item.description: Proven techniques for checking information — the SIFT method, lateral reading, telling news from advertising, and verifying images. A facts-only practical guide.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Build Its First Nuclear Plant: $16.5 Billion EPC Deal With Rosatom
item.description: On 3 September 2026, Rosatom and KNPP signed an EPC contract for Kazakhstan's first nuclear plant. Two VVER-1200 units (2,400 MW) will be built on Lake Balkhash; Russia will finance ~85%.

item.title: Israel Has Targeted Ceasefire Negotiators: The Facts on Doha (2025) and Tehran (2024)
item.description: Two documented events: a 9 September 2025 strike on Hamas's negotiating leadership in Doha (six killed, Israel claimed responsibility), and the 31 July 2024 killing of Ismail Haniyeh in Tehran. Facts only, with balance.

item.title: The third wave of Uzbek migration: post-Soviet labor migration (1991–2010)
item.description: The economic labor migration that began after the USSR collapsed — mainly to Russia, then Kazakhstan and Korea. A neutral history with dates, estimated figures and sources.

item.title: Iran Sends Conditions to End Its War With the US via Qatar; Oil Tops $100
item.description: Per Iran's SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei, Tehran set three conditions to end the war: a halt to fighting on all fronts, release of frozen funds, and an end to the naval blockade. Oil crossed $100/barrel on 9 September.

item.title: Uzbekistan Draws 9.1 Million Foreign Visitors in Eight Months as Tourism Exports Hit $4.6 Billion
item.description: Foreign arrivals rose 21.1% to 9.1 million in January–August 2026. Tourism service exports grew 53.5% to $4.6 billion, and average spending per tourist reached $503.

item.title: Islam Karimov: the first president of independent Uzbekistan (1938–2016)
item.description: Born in Samarkand in 1938, Islam Karimov led the state from 1991 until 2016. His biography, rule and contested events — a neutral, sourced history with dates.

item.title: Bank accounts and credit history in the USA: basics for newcomers
item.description: Opening a bank account, the difference between an SSN and an ITIN, FICO credit scores, and building credit from scratch — a facts-only guide for immigrants in the USA.

item.title: Kazakhstan Offers Canada a $255 Million Export Package
item.description: On 16 September 2026, the trade ministers of Kazakhstan and Canada discussed a list of potential exports across 45 product categories and a joint economic action plan in a phone call.

item.title: U.S.–Uzbekistan Trade Tops $1 Billion: Washington Deals and New Investment
item.description: Bilateral trade reached $881 million in 2024 (+15%) and exceeded $1 billion in 2025. At the 6 November 2025 Washington meeting, deals on Boeing aircraft, critical minerals and agriculture were announced.

item.title: Central Asia's Regional Organizations Explained: SCO, CIS, EAEU, CSTO, ECO and OTS
item.description: A facts-based reference on the main organizations the Central Asian states belong to — the SCO, CIS, Eurasian Economic Union, CSTO, ECO and the Organization of Turkic States — their founding dates, members and Uzbekistan's status.

item.title: The Changed Aral: A Dried Sea, a Saxaul Forest, and the Aral School in Nukus
item.description: The Aral Sea has lost about 90% of its size, and a new desert, the Aralkum, has formed in its place. Now a forest is being planted on the dried seabed, and ACDF has opened the Aral School residency in Nukus.

item.title: The First Years of Independent Uzbekistan: Building the State (1991–1994)
item.description: After the 31 August 1991 declaration of independence — the 29 December referendum, state symbols, the 1992 Constitution, UN membership and the introduction of the national som. A factual history with dates and figures.

item.title: What Remittances Are and Why They Matter: An Explainer for Uzbekistan
item.description: What a remittance is, the channels money moves through, the global scale, and the numbers for Uzbekistan (Central Bank and World Bank data) — a facts-based explainer.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Is Building Its First GDP-Compliant State Pharmaceutical Warehouse
item.description: On 16 September 2026, construction began in Bishkek of the country's first GDP-standard state pharmaceutical warehouse and logistics complex for Kyrgyzpharmatsiya. Total investment is 650 million som.

item.title: The Second Wave of the Uzbek Diaspora: World War II and Post-War Emigration (1940–1960)
item.description: Wartime captivity, displaced persons, and the formation of Uzbek-Turkestani communities in the US, Turkey and Saudi Arabia — a neutral, factual history with dates and sources.

item.title: Central Asian States Are Expanding Domestic Drone Production
item.description: Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan are ramping up domestic UAV production to reduce dependence on foreign suppliers.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and China Move Toward Mutual Recognition of Organic Product Certification
item.description: On 17 September in Bishkek, meeting a SAMR delegation, the two countries reached a principled agreement to work toward mutual recognition of organic certification systems. The aim is to simplify Kyrgyz organic exports to China.

item.title: The Basics of Islamic (Halal) Finance: What Riba Is and How the System Works
item.description: A facts-based explainer on the prohibition of riba (interest), the core principles and instruments of Islamic finance — murabaha, ijara, mudaraba, sukuk — its global scale, and Uzbekistan's steps in this direction.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Independence: The Road to 31 August 1991
item.description: From the Declaration of Sovereignty (1990) to the declaration of independence on 31 August 1991 and the December referendum — a factual history with dates, figures and the first steps of nation-building.

item.title: The First Wave of the Uzbek Diaspora: Emigration in 1917–1934
item.description: The political-refugee wave that followed the Russian Revolution, the fall of Bukhara and Khiva, the Basmachi movement and forced collectivization — a factual history of how the Uzbek and Turkestani diaspora took shape.

item.title: How Labor Migration Actually Works: The Rules for Russia, Korea and Europe
item.description: An explainer on the three main legal routes for Uzbek labor migrants — Russia's patent system, South Korea's EPS program and organized recruitment — how each is structured, its rules and its numbers.

item.title: Timur Turlov Runs for FIDE President: He Outlines His Platform at the Samarkand Olympiad
item.description: The 46th Chess Olympiad is under way in Samarkand, and the FIDE presidential election is set for 26 September. Timur Turlov is running on a ticket with Viswanathan Anand and has laid out a platform focused on education, technology and calendar stability.

item.title: Kazakh National University of Sports Joins Global Olympic Studies Network — First in Central Asia
item.description: The Astana-based university has joined the IOC-coordinated academic network of Olympic studies and will set up a Center for Olympic Studies, Education and Legacy.

item.title: Kazakhstan Postpones New Royalty System for Solid Minerals to 2029
item.description: The government moves the royalty from 1 January 2027 to 1 January 2029. Several technical questions remain unresolved.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Is Cleaning Up the Soviet-Era Mailuu-Suu Uranium Legacy
item.description: Central Asia's largest uranium legacy site holds about 2 million cubic metres of radioactive waste. With an EBRD grant, remediation is set to run through 2032.

item.title: Five Activists Sentenced in Almaty: 5 to 5.5 Years in the Alleged "Akorda Seizure" Case
item.description: The Almaly district court delivered its verdict on 8 September. Prosecutors had asked for eight years each; the hearings were held behind closed doors.

item.title: FIDE Elects Its President in Samarkand: Three Tickets and ~200 Federation Votes
item.description: The vote falls on 26 September at the FIDE General Assembly held alongside the 46th Chess Olympiad. Incumbent Arkady Dvorkovich suspended his powers in July after EU sanctions.
